advisories.title: table-level `PERMISSIONS FOR update` predicates referencing COMPUTED fields are evaluated before computed-field population, letting the predicate read `NONE` and always pass
advisories.summary:
> **affected**: SurrealDB `>= 3.2.0` (v2.x not assessed) - `UPDATE` (and the shared `check_update_permissions` / `recheck_update_permissions` gate)
> **dynamically reproduced**: official release binary **v3.2.0** and `master` `9d9a5b069` (v3.3.0-nightly), in-memory engine; control group run alongside (see PoC)

---

_Source references (`file.rs:line`) are to commit `9d9a5b069` (v3.3.0-nightly)._

### Summary

A table-level `PERMISSIONS FOR update` predicate that references a `COMPUTED` field is evaluated **before** that field is populated on the document, so the predicate observes `NONE` for the computed field regardless of the value the field would actually compute to. Any predicate of the form `WHERE computed_field <comparison> <literal>` that is meant to **deny** the caller can silently evaluate to truthy against `NONE` and let the update through. **Reproduced end-to-end: a record user `alice` was able to `UPDATE` a row whose table permission `FOR update WHERE blocked != true` should reject her, because `blocked` is `COMPUTED TRUE` and was `NONE` at permission-check time - while the identical predicate on a plain stored field correctly rejects.**

### Details

`Document::update` (`surrealdb/core/src/doc/update.rs:9-52`) runs its security gate at the very top:

```rust
// SECURITY: evaluate the table-level update permission BEFORE any
// user-supplied expression in the WHERE clause or data clause.
self.check_update_permissions(stk, ctx, opt, &self.current).await?;
```

At this point `self.current` is the document **as loaded from storage**; computed fields are only materialized later, in the output stage via `compute_fields` (`surrealdb/core/src/doc/compute.rs:56`). `check_update_permissions` (`surrealdb/core/src/doc/check.rs:389-401`) hands `self.current` to `process_permissions` (`check.rs:448-474`), which for `Permission::Specific(e)` computes the predicate against that `CursorDoc` with `Some(doc)` - so any computed field name inside `e` resolves via `Param::compute` / idiom lookup to `NONE` (the field is not in the doc yet).

The predicate `blocked != true` therefore sees `NONE != true` → `is_truthy()` → `Ok(())` → the update proceeds. The `recheck_update_permissions` call later (`update.rs:41`) is conditional on the permission being `Permission::Specific` (`check.rs:425-436`), but it too evaluates against `self.current` after `process_table_fields` - computed fields are populated on the *output/reduced* views, not guaranteed on the `self.current` view used for the permission re-check, so the gate is not closed there either.

The control group proves this is a timing bug, not a semantics decision: with `blocked` stored as a **plain field** (`CREATE person:1 SET blocked = true`), the same predicate `WHERE blocked != true` evaluates `true != true` → falsy → the update is **rejected**. Only the COMPUTED variant passes, and only because the predicate ran against an un-populated document.

`check_update_permissions` / `process_permissions` are shared by `UPDATE` (and the `CREATE`/`DELETE`/`SELECT` gates via `check_create_permissions` / `check_delete_permissions` / `check_select_permissions`), so the same class of bug affects any permission predicate that reads a computed field.

A self-contained, self-checking reproduction script is embedded below; it manages its own in-memory server, schema, record-access signup/signin, and asserts every step. Prereqs: a `surreal` binary built with `--features storage-mem,http`.

**Scope note**: dynamically reproduced on the **official v3.2.0 release binary** (`surreal-v3.2.0.linux-amd64.tgz`, 4/4 checks pass) and on `master` at commit `9d9a5b069` (v3.3.0-nightly, 4/4 checks pass). advisories.summary:
### Summary

`surrealdb-core` pins `reblessive 0.4.3` (crates.io, checksum `bbc4a4ea…e73c8c`) and uses its recursive-async runtime for every SurrealQL statement: `dbs::Executor` holds a `TreeStack` field and drives each statement through `self.stack.enter(|stk| s.compute(stk, &self.ctx, &self.opt, None)).finish().await`. `reblessive 0.4.3` unconditionally asserts `Send`/`Sync` for its runtime types (`unsafe impl Send/Sync for Stack`, `unsafe impl Send/Sync for TreeStack`, `unsafe impl<R> Send/Sync for Runner`), while its public entry points accept **any** future with no `Send` bound (`pub fn enter<'a, F, Fut, R>(&'a mut self, f: F) -> Runner<'a, R> where F: FnOnce(&'a mut Stk) -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = R> + 'a`) and store it type-erased (function-pointer vtable) in a bump allocator. Two safe-code consequences follow: (1) `Runner::step_async`/`finish_async` return `StepFuture<'a, R>`/`FinishFuture<'a, R>` whose lifetime is the stack borrow rather than `&mut self`, so driver futures can be duplicated; because `Stack: Sync`, those futures are `Send`, and two threads polling them run `drive_top_task(&self)` concurrently - racy `Cell`/`UnsafeCell` reads and writes, double `pop_task()`/`pop_dealloc()` (double drop / double free) and a non-atomic `Option<R>::take`; (2) `TreeStack: Send` lets safe code move a driver whose type-erased future captures `!Send` state (`Rc`, `RefCell`) to another thread while the creating thread keeps an alias of that state. ThreadSanitizer confirms 11 data races on the attached PoC (including on `reblessive`'s own `Cell<usize>`/`StackAllocator` state) and the corrupted allocator makes `reblessive` itself panic (`stack/mod.rs:177:54`, `Option::unwrap()` on `None`) in one case. No `unsafe` is needed at the call site. SurrealDB's own query futures stay `Send` only because of the unsound `unsafe impl Send for TreeStack`: the futures stored in `Executor`'s `TreeStack` capture `&mut tree::Stk`, and `tree::Stk` is deliberately `!Send` (`PhantomData<*mut TreeStack>`).

### Details

**Verified snapshot.** `surrealdb 3.3.0-nightly`, git commit `18971ffba781a796c0ad3897bb4b82432c241e4c` (2026-09-04), crate `surrealdb-core 3.3.0-nightly`. Dependency `reblessive 0.4.3` (crates.io, checksum `bbc4a4ea2a66a41a1152c4b3d86e8954dc087bdf33af35446e6e176db4e73c8c`), declared at workspace `Cargo.toml:94` and `surrealdb/core/Cargo.toml:95` (`reblessive = { workspace = true, features = ["tree"] }`). We verified only this snapshot; any release that resolves `reblessive 0.4.3` with these sources is affected - please set the final affected/patched ranges when publishing. As of 2026-09-21, crates.io's newest `reblessive` is still 0.4.3 and the upstream repository (`github.com/DelSkayn/reblessive`, maintained by a SurrealDB core developer) still carries the same `unsafe impl`s on its `main` branch; no fix is staged.

advisories.title: Surrealism WASI socket allowlist ignores deny_net, enabling SSRF via hostname resolving to a private IP
advisories.summary:
## Summary

SurrealDB's Surrealism WASM plugin runtime builds the outbound network allowlist for guest WASI Preview 2 sockets from a module's declared `allow_net` entries without ever re-checking the resolved IP addresses against the server's `deny_net` policy or against private, loopback, and link-local ranges. An authenticated principal who can load and invoke a Surrealism module (with the experimental `surrealism` capability enabled) can declare `allow_net = ["attacker-controlled-hostname"]` whose DNS record points at a forbidden address such as a cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), a loopback service (127.0.0.1), or an RFC1918 host. Load-time validation inspects the entry only as a host string and admits it; the runtime then resolves the hostname and stores the resulting private or denied IP directly in the guest socket filter, so guest WASM can open a raw TCP or UDP connection to an operator-forbidden internal endpoint. This is server-side request forgery over arbitrary TCP and UDP protocols and ports, defeating the exact `deny_net` egress guard that several prior SurrealDB SSRF advisories were published to enforce.

## Root Cause

SurrealDB enforces outbound network policy through an allow-list combined with a deny-list (`Capabilities::allows_network_target` = `allow_net.matches(target) && !deny_net.matches(target)`). For the reqwest-based HTTP and JWKS clients this policy is completed at DNS time by `FilteringResolver`, which re-checks each resolved IP against the deny-list and private-IP ranges. The Surrealism raw-socket path has no equivalent re-check, and load-time validation compares only host strings, so a hostname that resolves to a denied or private IP is never blocked.

Two independent gaps combine:

1. Load-time validation is string-only. `validate_surrealism_capabilities` checks each `allow_net` entry via `NetTarget::from_str` and `allows_network_target`. An IP-range `deny_net` entry is a `NetTarget::IPNet`; matching it against a domain target (`NetTarget::Host(Domain)`) falls through to the `_ => false` arm of `NetTarget::matches`, so the deny-list never matches a hostname. A literal-IP `allow_net` entry would be rejected here, but a hostname is admitted.
2. Runtime resolution has no deny or private-IP filter. `resolve_allow_net` resolves the admitted hostname to its IP and stores `ResolvedNetAllow::Net(<resolved IP>)` (portless entries match on any port). The WASI socket gate installed by `wasi_context::build` (`socket_addr_check`) admits an outbound connection whenever any allow filter matches the destination, with no consultation of `deny_net` or private-IP ranges.

```text
Affected components (repository-relative paths):
- surrealism/runtime/src/net_allow.rs
    resolve_allow_net / resolve_hostname (lines 46-107): resolves module allow_net
    hostnames to IPs and stores them for the WASI allowlist with no deny/private filter;
    ResolvedNetAllow::matches_socket_addr (lines 20-27) is allow-only and ignores port.
- surrealism/runtime/src/wasi_context.rs
    build (lines 114-155): installs socket_addr_check (lines 137-146) that admits any
    outbound connect matching an allow filter, with no deny_net/private-IP gate, and
    leaves TCP/UDP enabled for a non-empty allowlist.
- surrealdb/core/src/dbs/capabilities.rs
    validate_surrealism_capabilities (lines 1006-1057): string-only load check;
    NetTarget::matches (lines 261-284) returns false for an IPNet deny entry against a
    Host(Domain) target, so a hostname resolving to a denied IP passes.
```

## Impact

An attacker who can load and invoke a Surrealism module against a server with the experimental `surrealism` capability enabled can cause the server to open raw TCP and UDP connections to endpoints the operator explicitly forbade through `deny_net`. advisories.title: VIEWER role can define tables implicitly via CREATE on a non-STRICT database
advisories.summary:
**Version:** `surreal version`: 3.2.0 for linux on x86_64. Seen first on a RocksDB-backed server, reproduced on an in-memory one.

**Summary:** a user with the `VIEWER` role can change a database's schema. `CREATE` on a table that does not exist yet, in a database that is not `STRICT`, returns `OK` and leaves a new table defined as `TYPE ANY SCHEMALESS PERMISSIONS NONE` (0 rows). An explicit `DEFINE TABLE` by the same user is correctly refused ("IAM error: Not enough permissions to perform this action"), so the implicit definition bypasses the check that the explicit one applies.

**Reproduce** (fresh server: `surreal start --user root --pass root memory`):

As root:
```sql
DEFINE NAMESPACE n; USE NS n; DEFINE DATABASE loose; DEFINE DATABASE strict STRICT;
DEFINE USER v ON ROOT PASSWORD 'v' ROLES VIEWER;
USE NS n DB loose; DEFINE TABLE t SCHEMALESS; CREATE t:1 SET a = 1;
```
As `v` (ns `n`, db `loose`):
```sql
CREATE probe_new:x SET a = 1;   -- OK, returns []
DEFINE TABLE probe_defined;     -- ERR: IAM error: Not enough permissions
UPDATE t:1 SET a = 2;           -- OK, returns [], row unchanged (expected)
```
As root: `INFO FOR DB;` now lists `probe_new` (`DEFINE TABLE probe_new TYPE ANY SCHEMALESS PERMISSIONS NONE`), 0 rows.
In db `strict` the same `CREATE` by `v` returns "The table 'probe_new' does not exist" (expected).

**Impact:** a read-only credential (e.g. one given to a backup or reporting job) can add arbitrary empty tables to any non-STRICT database it can reach. No data is read or changed beyond that, but it is a schema write by a role documented as read-only, and it can clutter or collide with table names an application later defines.

**Expected:** a `VIEWER` statement that would implicitly define a table is refused the same way an explicit `DEFINE TABLE` is.

**Workaround we plan:** set every database reachable by VIEWER users to STRICT.

### Patches

A patch has been created that requires DEFINE TABLE authority before a table is defined on demand, so a VIEWER can no longer implicitly create a table via CREATE on a nonexistent table.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE TABLE](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/table)
- `fix(exec): require DEFINE TABLE authority to define a table on demand` (commit `2598b3b0ad`)

advisories.title: Server crash (DoS) via decimal overflow in math::sum / math::product
advisories.summary:
### Summary

An uncaught arithmetic overflow in the `math::sum` and `math::product` aggregate functions lets any user who can run a single query terminate the entire SurrealDB server process. When the running total of a `decimal` accumulation exceeds the `decimal` range, the worker thread panics inside `rust_decimal` instead of returning an error, and the process exits (status 133). Every connection, database and namespace on the instance goes down with it. No special privileges, no large dataset, and no stored data are required - the overflowing values can be literals in the query. Confirmed on `3.2.4` and `3.1.2`.

### Details

`math::sum` and `math::product` accumulate their arguments using unchecked `decimal` arithmetic. When an intermediate result exceeds the `decimal` maximum (`79228162514264337593543950335`), the addition panics rather than returning a `Result::Err`, and the panic aborts the SurrealDB worker thread, which terminates the whole server process.

The engine already has a correct, recoverable path for exactly this condition:

- The `+` and `*` **operators** on the same operands return a normal query error  (`Cannot perform addition with '...' and '...'`).
- `math::mean`, which also sums internally, returns that same error rather than panicking.

So only the `math::sum` / `math::product` accumulation escalates an out-of-range decimal to a process-killing panic. The fix is to have these functions use the same checked arithmetic the operators and `math::mean` already use.

Source pointer for the maintainer:
The chain, with line numbers from `main` at commit `18971ffba` (the 3.1.x / 3.2.x release tags differ by a few lines but the structure is identical):

- `surrealdb/core/src/fnc/math.rs:218` - `math::sum`:
  ```rust
  pub fn sum((array,): (Vec<Number>,)) -> Result<Value> {
      Ok(array.into_iter().sum::<Number>().into())
  }
  ```
  and `:182` - `math::product` via `product::<Number>()`.
- `surrealdb/core/src/val/number.rs:1160` - `impl Sum for Number` folds with the plain operator:
  `iter.fold(Number::Int(0), |a, b| a + b)` (and `:1178`, `Product`, folds with `*`).
- `surrealdb/core/src/val/number.rs:1034` - `impl ops::Add for Number`, whose decimal arm is **unchecked**:
  ```rust
  (Number::Decimal(v), Number::Decimal(w)) => Number::Decimal(v + w),
  ```
  `v + w` here is `rust_decimal`'s `Decimal + Decimal`, which panics on overflow - the frame in the crash log is `rust_decimal-1.42.0/src/arithmetic_impls.rs:161:18`,  `Addition overflowed`.



### PoC

Start a server with the in-memory backend (any 3.1.x / 3.2.x build):

```bash
surreal start --user root --pass root memory
```

Send a single statement over the HTTP `/sql` endpoint:

```bash
curl -s -u root:root \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' -H 'surreal-ns: t' -H 'surreal-db: t' \
  -X POST --data 'RETURN math::sum([40000000000000000000000000000dec, 40000000000000000000000000000dec]);' \
  http://localhost:8000/sql
```

The connection is dropped with no query result. The server log shows:

```
thread 'surrealdb-worker' (8) panicked at .../rust_decimal-1.42.0/src/arithmetic_impls.rs:161:18:
Addition overflowed
```

and the process exits with status 133. Any subsequent request to the same server fails
(the process is gone).

Equivalent triggers, all fatal:

```surql
RETURN math::sum([79228162514264337593543950335dec, 1dec]);   -- decimal max + 1
RETURN math::sum([79228162514264337593543950335dec, 1]);      -- mixed int addend
RETURN math::sum([-40000000000000000000000000000dec, -40000000000000000000000000000dec]);
RETURN math::product([40000000000000000000000000000dec, 2dec]);
```

Reachable through ordinary aggregation, so a routine reporting query over a table holding
large decimals is an accidental trigger:

```surql
CREATE t:1 SET v = 40000000000000000000000000000dec;
CREATE t:2 SET v = 40000000000000000000000000000dec;
SELECT math::sum(v) AS s FROM t GROUP ALL;   -- se...

advisories.title: Quoted Computed-Field Formatter Bypasses Field-Level SELECT Permissions
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A field-level authorization bypass exists in SurrealDB's query execution engine (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/core/src/exec/operators/scan/pipeline.rs`, computed field names are escaped with backticks prior to object insertion, mismatching permission filters.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected File: `surrealdb/core/src/exec/operators/scan/pipeline.rs` (`build_field_state_raw`, `compute_fields_for_value`)
- Mechanism: Computed fields format their names with `fd.name.to_raw_string()`, which automatically surrounds hyphenated or special identifiers with backticks (e.g., `private-data` becomes `` `private-data` ``). When inserted into the document, the key contains backticks, whereas the schema permission validator checks the raw unescaped name (`private-data`). The permission check fails to match and allows the field to be returned to unauthorized users.
- Impact: Unauthorized disclosure of restricted computed fields.

### Recommended Remediation
Use unquoted raw field names for computed field dictionary keys during document evaluation and projection.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created in the 4.0 execution engine that keys computed fields by their raw, unescaped identifier, so a quoted (backtick-escaped) computed-field name no longer mismatches the field-level SELECT permission and leaks the field.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE FIELD](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/field)
- `fix(exec): derive the computed fields a field's SELECT clause reads in its own frame` (commit `d813af6632`)
- `test(doc,catalog): pin quoted and nested field names in write gates and field clauses` (commit `bf6a742fd8`)

advisories.title: Direct Filesystem Buckets Permit Path Traversal Across Key-Based ACL Boundaries
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A path traversal vulnerability exists in SurrealDB's direct filesystem bucket implementation (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/core/src/buc/controller.rs` and `store/file.rs`, key permissions are checked against the un-normalized object key, but the backend path collapses `..` sequences via path cleaning.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected Files: `surrealdb/core/src/buc/controller.rs` (`BucketController::check_permission`), `surrealdb/core/src/buc/store/file.rs` (`FileStore::to_os_path`)
- Mechanism: Access control policy verifies the requested object key before resolution. However, `FileStore::to_os_path` normalizes relative directory components via `.clean()` without calling `check_no_traversal` (which is only present on `PrefixedStore`). A tenant authorized only for keys within `/public/` can supply a key such as `/public/../private/confidential.txt`, which passes permission evaluation and resolves to arbitrary files within the storage root.
- Impact: Unauthorized read, write, and deletion of files outside permitted key boundaries.

### Recommended Remediation
Enforce strict traversal checking (`check_no_traversal`) on all direct `FileStore` key inputs prior to permission evaluation and file system operations.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that runs the traversal check on the key itself for a direct `file://` bucket, so a `..` key can no longer cross the bucket's key-based ACL boundary.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- `fix(buc): filesystem bucket path traversal via symlinks, Windows backslashes, and direct-bucket keys` (commit `5edf982bf0`)

advisories.title: Windows Backslashes Bypass Global Bucket Path Traversal Protection
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A path traversal bypass exists on Windows platforms within SurrealDB's bucket storage layer (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/core/src/buc/store/path.rs`, traversal validation splits only on forward slashes (`/`), ignoring backslashes (`\`).

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected Files: `surrealdb/core/src/buc/store/path.rs` (`ObjectKey::check_no_traversal`), `surrealdb/core/src/buc/store/file.rs` (`FileStore::to_os_path`)
- Mechanism: `ObjectKey::check_no_traversal` validates path components by splitting exclusively on `/`. When deployed on Windows hosts, `FileStore::to_os_path` utilizes the operating system path separator where `\` represents directory hierarchy. An object key such as `/..\bucket2\secret` bypasses forward-slash validation, yet is interpreted as directory traversal during OS file path resolution.
- Impact: Cross-bucket file disclosure and modification on Windows installations.

### Recommended Remediation
Normalize path separators or reject keys containing `\` in `check_no_traversal` before path resolution.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that treats a backslash as a path separator when checking a bucket key for traversal, closing the Windows backslash bypass.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- `fix(buc): filesystem bucket path traversal via symlinks, Windows backslashes, and direct-bucket keys` (commit `5edf982bf0`)

advisories.title: Filesystem Bucket Containment Fails to Resolve Descendant Symlinks
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A symbolic link traversal vulnerability exists in SurrealDB's filesystem storage bucket (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/core/src/buc/store/file.rs`, containment assertions only canonicalize the bucket root rather than resolving descendant symlinks.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected File: `surrealdb/core/src/buc/store/file.rs` (`to_os_path`, `get`, `put`, `copy`, `rename`, `list`)
- Mechanism: The security assertion checks `path.starts_with(&self.root)` using lexical comparison. If the storage directory contains a pre-existing symbolic link pointing outside the bucket root (e.g. `<root>/link -> /etc`), requests referencing `/link/secret` satisfy the prefix check and allow arbitrary file reads and writes across the host filesystem.
- Impact: Host filesystem disclosure and modification via symlink navigation.

### Recommended Remediation
Fully canonicalize the final target path using `std::fs::canonicalize()` and verify that the canonical path resides within the canonical bucket root.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that canonicalizes the deepest existing ancestor of a filesystem bucket key and re-checks it against the canonical root, so an in-bucket symlink can no longer redirect an operation outside the bucket root.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- `fix(buc): filesystem bucket path traversal via symlinks, Windows backslashes, and direct-bucket keys` (commit `5edf982bf0`)

advisories.title: REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE/UNSET/CUSTOM bypasses target table PERMISSIONS FOR delete/update
advisories.summary:
## Summary

In SurrealDB, when a record is deleted that is referenced by fields defined with `DEFINE FIELD ... REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE`, `ON DELETE UNSET`, or `ON DELETE CUSTOM`, the cascade operation on the referencing table executes with permissions unconditionally suppressed. An authenticated user who can delete a record on the referenced table can trigger unauthorized deletion, modification, or expression execution on records in a referencing table, even when that table has `PERMISSIONS FOR delete NONE` or `PERMISSIONS FOR update NONE`.

## Root Cause

The function `Document::purge_references` in `surrealdb/core/src/doc/purge.rs` unconditionally disables permission checks before executing cascade operations on referencing tables. This violates the security invariant documented in `SECURITY_GUIDE.md` (lines 141-143): "When system-internal code paths (events, views, cascades) set `perms=false`, this suppression must not extend to user-supplied expressions or user-controlled data lookups beyond the strictly required scope."

```rust
// CASCADE path (purge.rs:376):
stm.compute(stk, ctx, &opt.clone().with_perms(false), None)

// UNSET path (purge.rs:385):
let opt = opt.clone().with_perms(false);

// CUSTOM path (purge.rs:453):
let opt = opt.clone().with_perms(false);
```

The `with_perms(false)` call sets the `perms` field on the `Options` struct to `false`. When the cascade DELETE or UPDATE later calls `check_perms` (at `surrealdb/core/src/ctx/context.rs:612-614`), the function returns `Ok(false)` immediately without evaluating the target table's `PERMISSIONS` clause:

```rust
pub fn check_perms(&self, opt: &Options, action: Action) -> Result<bool> {
    if !opt.perms {
        return Ok(false);
    }
    // ... remaining permission logic never reached
}
```

The parallel function `purge_edges` (purge.rs:186-232) was fixed in v3.1.0 (CVE-2026-49997, GHSA-whwg-vh4f-pmmf) to preserve the caller's `opt` and thus respect edge table permissions. The comment at purge.rs:222-227 explicitly documents this security requirement. `purge_references` retains the pre-fix pattern at all three cascade sites.

## Impact

An authenticated user with DELETE permission on a referenced table (e.g., `user`) can:

- **CASCADE**: Delete all records in a referencing table (e.g., `audit_log`) that point to the deleted record, bypassing `PERMISSIONS FOR delete NONE` on that table.
- **UNSET**: Modify records in a referencing table by clearing reference fields, bypassing `PERMISSIONS FOR update NONE`.
- **CUSTOM**: Execute admin-defined expressions against records in a referencing table with system-level privileges, bypassing all PERMISSIONS clauses.

This requires an administrator to have configured `DEFINE FIELD ... REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE|UNSET|CUSTOM` on the referencing table. This is a documented, production-intended feature for referential integrity. The administrator who defines both a REFERENCE cascade and restrictive PERMISSIONS expects both policies to be enforced.

The attacker cannot cross namespace or database isolation boundaries, and cannot delete records on tables where they lack DELETE permission on the referenced endpoint. The primitive is reliable and deterministic: a single DELETE statement triggers the cascade.

Setup: root access to define schema, then switch to a record-scoped access user.
```

DEFINE TABLE user SCHEMALESS
    PERMISSIONS FOR select, create, delete FULL;

DEFINE TABLE audit_log SCHEMALESS

advisories.summary:
The `--help` and `-h` output of seven commands shows the current values of credential environment variables in clear text:

| Command | Values in the help output |
|---|---|
| `surreal start` | `SURREAL_PASS` |
| `surreal sql` | `SURREAL_PASS`, `SURREAL_TOKEN` |
| `surreal import` | `SURREAL_PASS`, `SURREAL_TOKEN` |
| `surreal export` | `SURREAL_PASS`, `SURREAL_TOKEN` |
| `surreal mcp` | `SURREAL_PASS` |
| `surreal ml import` | `SURREAL_PASS`, `SURREAL_TOKEN` |
| `surreal ml export` | `SURREAL_PASS`, `SURREAL_TOKEN` |

Versions: we reproduced this on seven official Docker images: `v2.7.0`, `v3.2.0`, `v3.2.4`, `v3.2.5`, `v3.3.0`, `v3.3.2`, and `v3.3.4`. The last one reports `3.3.4 for linux on x86_64`. Version 2.7.0 does not have the `mcp` command. We did not run other 2.x versions or versions before 2.7.0.

Steps to reproduce:

```sh
docker run --rm -e SURREAL_PASS=example-password -e SURREAL_TOKEN=example-token \
  surrealdb/surrealdb:v3.3.4 export --help | grep -E 'SURREAL_(PASS|TOKEN)='
```

Output:

```text
          [env: SURREAL_PASS=example-password]
          [env: SURREAL_TOKEN=example-token]
```

Impact: in container deployments, the server credentials are usually in the environment of the server container. A Kubernetes Secret or `docker run -e` puts them there. An operator can run `surreal export --help` or `surreal sql --help` in that container, for example with `kubectl exec`. The root password then goes to the terminal output. Terminal output can go to shell logs, CI logs, screen shares, and support tickets. Operators do not expect a secret in help output, so they do not protect it. This is not a privilege escalation, because a person who can run commands in the container can also read its environment. The risk is accidental disclosure.

Cause: clap shows the value of an `env` variable in the help text unless the argument sets `hide_env_values = true`. These arguments do not set it. The line numbers are for tag `v3.3.0`, and the `surrealdb-server` 3.3.4 crate has the same files:

- `surrealdb/server/src/cli/abstraction/mod.rs`, line 19: `env = "SURREAL_PASS"` on `password`. The `sql`, `import`, `export`, `ml import`, and `ml export` commands use this argument.
- `surrealdb/server/src/cli/abstraction/mod.rs`, line 28: `env = "SURREAL_TOKEN"` on `token`. The same five commands use this argument.
- `surrealdb/server/src/cli/start.rs`, line 195: `env = "SURREAL_PASS"` on the `password` of the `start` command.
- `surrealdb/server/src/cli/mcp.rs`, line 52: `env = "SURREAL_PASS"` on the `password` of the `mcp` command.

At tags `v1.0.0` and `v2.0.0`, the `password` argument in `src/cli/abstraction/mod.rs` also does not set `hide_env_values`.

Suggested fix: set `hide_env_values = true` on each of the four arguments above. These four changes cover all seven commands. The help text then shows `[env: SURREAL_PASS]` without the value. For example, the `password` argument in `abstraction/mod.rs` becomes:

```rust
#[arg(
    env = "SURREAL_PASS",
    hide_env_values = true,
    short = 'p',
    long = "password",
    visible_alias = "pass",
    requires = "username"
)]
pub(crate) password: Option<String>,
```

The `token` argument in the same file, and the `password` arguments in `start.rs` and `mcp.rs`, get the same added line.

We did not include `SURREAL_KEY` in `start.rs`, because it sets `hide = true`. `SURREAL_KVS_KEY` and `SURREAL_WEB_KEY` hold file paths, not secret values.

If you do not think that this is a vulnerability, please tell us, and we will open a public issue instead.

An AI coding agent (Claude Code) ran the reproduction and drafted this report. I examined the results before I sent it.

### Patches

A patch has been created that redacts the values of SURREAL_PASS and SURREAL_TOKEN from the CLI `--help` output.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

advisories.title: GraphQL WebSocket upgrade omits frame and message size limits enabling memory amplification
advisories.summary:
## Summary

The SurrealDB server's GraphQL WebSocket endpoint at `GET /graphql` upgrades incoming connections without applying any of the operator-configurable frame, message, or buffer size limits (`SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`, `SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_READ_BUFFER_SIZE`, `SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE`, `SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_MAX_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE`) that are applied to the `/rpc` and `/sql` upgrade handlers. As a result the endpoint inherits the underlying tungstenite library's permissive defaults (16 MiB per frame, 64 MiB per message, unbounded write buffer) regardless of what the operator configured. For any deployment that has `DEFINE CONFIG GRAPHQL` set on at least one database, an unauthenticated network client that supplies the target namespace and database in request headers can hold up to 64 MiB of in-flight bytes per concurrent connection, exhausting server memory and degrading availability for every endpoint served by the same process.

## Root Cause

The server exposes three WebSocket upgrade handlers under different HTTP routes. The handlers for `/rpc` and `/sql` explicitly propagate the shared `WEBSOCKET_*` capacity constants onto the axum `WebSocketUpgrade`, so the underlying tungstenite `WebSocketConfig` observes the operator's configured limits before any bytes are accepted from the socket. The GraphQL WebSocket handler does not perform any of those calls, so tungstenite falls back to its library defaults (max frame size 16 MiB, max message size 64 MiB, max write buffer `usize::MAX`) even when the operator has explicitly lowered `SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`. The security invariant that "operator-configured per-connection frame and buffer limits apply to every WebSocket endpoint the server exposes" is violated because the GraphQL upgrade builder never binds any of those constants.

The affected upgrade path is the `GET` handler registered in `server/src/ntw/graphql.rs`:

```rust
// server/src/ntw/graphql.rs:23-72 (relevant excerpt)
pub fn router() -> Router<Arc<RpcState>> {
    Router::new().route("/graphql", get(ws_handler).post_service(GraphQLService::new()))
}

async fn ws_handler(
    ws: WebSocketUpgrade,
    ...
) -> impl IntoResponse {
    // ... capability + session checks ...
    ws.protocols(ALL_WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOLS).on_upgrade(move |socket| async move {
        serve_graphql_ws(socket, schema, protocol, data).await;
    })
}
```

For contrast, the sibling handler at `server/src/ntw/sql.rs:105-115` binds all five limits before `on_upgrade`:

```rust
ws
    .max_frame_size(*WEBSOCKET_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE)
    .max_message_size(*WEBSOCKET_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE)
    .read_buffer_size(*WEBSOCKET_READ_BUFFER_SIZE)
    .write_buffer_size(*WEBSOCKET_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE)
    .max_write_buffer_size(*WEBSOCKET_MAX_WRITE_BUFFER_SIZE)
    .on_failed_upgrade(...)
    .on_upgrade(move |socket| handle_socket(state, socket, sess))
```

The equivalent binding block is present at `server/src/ntw/rpc.rs:110-122` and absent from `server/src/ntw/graphql.rs`. The `cnf::WEBSOCKET_*` constants (and any operator override sourced from `SURREAL_WEBSOCKET_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`) are never referenced from the GraphQL upgrade file.

## Impact

Any deployment that ships the default `graphql` feature and has configured at least one database with `DEFINE CONFIG GRAPHQL` is exposed. No credentials are required to reach the vulnerable upgrade: the server's auth middleware silently produces an anonymous session when neither `Authorization: Basic` nor `Authorization: Bearer` is presented, and the GraphQL schema generation path opens a raw read transaction without invoking `check_anon` or any related capability check. The attacker only needs the namespace and database names, which are typically application configuration rather than secrets.

advisories.title: MCP Tool Identifier Validation Permits Statement Injection via Escaped Backticks
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A SQL statement injection vulnerability exists in SurrealDB's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server integration (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/mcp/src/tools/mod.rs`, discrepancy between identifier validation and SQL lexing permits delimiter escape.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected Files: `surrealdb/mcp/src/tools/mod.rs` (`consume_backtick_ident`, `validate_identifier`), `surrealdb/mcp/src/tools/crud.rs`
- Mechanism: The MCP identifier validator treats the first backtick as the closing identifier delimiter regardless of preceding escape characters (`\`). However, SurrealQL's SQL parser recognizes `\`` as an escaped literal backtick within an identifier. Passing an identifier containing an escaped backtick allows an attacker to break out of the quoted identifier into raw SurrealQL statement execution.
- Impact: Arbitrary SQL query execution through MCP tool invocation, bypassing tool argument constraints.

### Recommended Remediation
Synchronize MCP identifier parsing with the core SurrealQL lexer to handle escape characters correctly, or construct queries using parameterized AST nodes instead of string interpolation.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that validates MCP tool identifiers so an escaped backtick can no longer break out of the identifier and inject a statement.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- `fix(mcp): MCP tool identifier validation permits statement injection via escaped backticks` (commit `ec41ae8f15`)

# Authenticated Export Permission Bypass

## Summary

At revision `18971ffba781a796c0ad3897bb4b82432c241e4c`, an authenticated database-view caller can invoke `GET /export` and receive raw records without the table `SELECT` predicate or field-level `SELECT` projection enforced by the same caller's `/sql` session. A pinned runtime comparison with a database JWT carrying `AC=low` and `RL=[]` returned a non-empty export containing a non-owner row and a `SELECT NONE` field, while same-token SQL returned only the owner-visible row and an unrestricted control row. This demonstrates a confidentiality bypass at the exact tested revision; no broader release range is inferred.

## Technical Details

The HTTP export handler in `surrealdb/server/src/ntw/export.rs` checks the route capability, requires a namespace and database, authorizes database `View`, and calls `db.export_with_config(&session, ...)`. `Datastore::export_with_config` creates a read-only transaction and dispatches to the export implementation in `surrealdb/core/src/kvs/export.rs`.

The export chain reaches `export_table_data` and `export_regular_data`. The latter scans raw key/value records, decodes each value, and emits an `INSERT` statement. That path does not evaluate the requesting session's table `SELECT` predicate or apply the field-level permission filter before serialization. The `/sql` path uses the same session, checks table visibility during record resolution, and filters fields before returning them. Consequently, the two supported read surfaces expose different data to the same authenticated principal.

The following fixture is executed by the PoC as the root database administrator after selecting namespace `lab` and database `db`:

CREATE public:control SET marker = 'export-control';

-- RL:[] so the caller is database-scoped but has no built-in Viewer role.

advisories.title: JavaScript Built-in Bridge Bypasses Function Capability Enforcement
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A capability check bypass exists in SurrealDB's embedded JavaScript scripting engine (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/core/src/fnc/script/modules/surrealdb/functions/mod.rs`, JavaScript bridges call internal dispatchers directly without verifying function permissions.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected File: `surrealdb/core/src/fnc/script/modules/surrealdb/functions/mod.rs` (`run()`, `fut()`)
- Mechanism: SurrealQL enforces fine-grained function capabilities via `Function::compute()` and `BuiltinFunctionExec::evaluate()`. However, the JavaScript bridge `surrealdb.functions.*` calls `fnc::synchronous()` and `fnc::asynchronous()` directly, skipping capability checks. An unprivileged user denied access to sensitive built-in functions in SurrealQL can execute them arbitrarily via embedded JavaScript functions.
- Impact: Bypass of function authorization restrictions in scripted execution environments.

### Recommended Remediation
Enforce capability checks (`check_function_capability()`) inside the JavaScript function bridge before delegating to internal function dispatchers.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that enforces function-capability checks inside the embedded JavaScript built-in bridge, so a denied built-in function can no longer be reached from script.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- [SurrealQL Documentation - Scripting functions](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/functions/script)
- `fix(script): JS bridge bypasses the query and function capabilities` (commit `0b8be14543`)

advisories.title: JavaScript Query Bridge Bypasses Arbitrary-Query Subject Gate
advisories.summary:
### Summary
An authorization gate bypass exists in SurrealDB's JavaScript query module (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/core/src/fnc/script/modules/surrealdb/query/mod.rs`, the bridge executes queries without verifying the caller's query capability.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected File: `surrealdb/core/src/fnc/script/modules/surrealdb/query/mod.rs` (`query()`)
- Mechanism: SurrealDB uses `Capabilities::allows_query()` to gate subjects permitted to execute arbitrary queries. While nested queries in SurrealQL functions check this capability, the JavaScript `surrealdb.query()` bridge directly parses and executes input queries without checking `allows_query()`. A restricted subject permitted to run a specific script can bypass policy and execute arbitrary queries.
- Impact: Execution of unrestricted arbitrary queries by subjects restricted to predefined operations.

### Recommended Remediation
Validate `ctx.capabilities.allows_query()` in `surrealdb/query/mod.rs` before parsing and executing queries.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that enforces the query and function capabilities inside the embedded JavaScript bridge, so a script can no longer run arbitrary queries or functions that the session's capabilities deny.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- [SurrealQL Documentation - Scripting functions](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/functions/script)
- `fix(script): JS bridge bypasses the query and function capabilities` (commit `0b8be14543`)

SurrealDB DDL statements bypass namespace/database implicit-creation authorization added by GHSA-wp87-mgvq-5j93 fix
advisories.summary:
## Summary

Several DDL statements (DEFINE FUNCTION, DEFINE PARAM, DEFINE EVENT, DEFINE FIELD, DEFINE ANALYZER, DEFINE DATABASE, and others) can recreate a dropped namespace and database by reaching the same creation sinks that the GHSA-wp87-mgvq-5j93 fix gated for USE statements. A database-level Editor with an active WebSocket or embedded SDK session that was established before the namespace was dropped can execute a DDL statement and silently recreate the namespace without holding root-level DEFINE NAMESPACE permission.

## Root Cause

The GHSA-wp87-mgvq-5j93 fix added authorization checks (`should_materialize_ns_on_use` / `should_materialize_db_on_use`) to the three USE entry points (the SurrealQL executor, the RPC `yuse` method, and `Datastore::process_use`). These checks verify that the caller holds `is_allowed(Action::Edit, ResourceKind::Namespace.on_root())` before creating a missing namespace. However, the same creation sinks are reachable through Context wrapper functions called by DDL statements, and those wrappers perform no equivalent authorization check.

```text
Affected functions:
  Context::get_ns_db_ids  (surrealdb/core/src/ctx/context.rs:663)
    Calls ensure_ns_db without namespace-creation authorization.
    Called by: DEFINE FUNCTION (function.rs:55), DEFINE PARAM (param.rs:52),
              DEFINE EVENT (event.rs:47), DEFINE FIELD (field.rs:180),
              DEFINE ANALYZER (analyzer.rs:94), and other DB-level DDL.

  Context::get_ns_id  (surrealdb/core/src/ctx/context.rs:640)
    Calls get_or_add_ns without namespace-creation authorization.
    Called by: DEFINE USER ON NS (user.rs:172) and related NS-level DDL.

Creation sink:
  get_or_add_db_upwards (surrealdb/core/src/kvs/tx.rs:2468) with upwards=true
    calls get_or_add_ns (catalog/providers.rs:109) which creates a
    NamespaceDefinition in the KV store when the namespace does not exist.
```

## Impact

A database-level or namespace-level Editor can recreate a namespace that a root administrator deliberately dropped, provided they hold an active in-memory session (WebSocket or embedded SDK) that was authenticated before the namespace removal. The attacker cannot create arbitrary new namespaces; they can only recreate the specific namespace associated with their session. The recreated namespace is empty (it receives a new internal namespace ID, so old data is not exposed).

This crosses the root authorization boundary: namespace creation requires `is_allowed(Action::Edit, ResourceKind::Namespace.on_root())` per the GHSA-wp87-mgvq-5j93 fix, but a database-level Editor does not hold that permission. In multi-tenant deployments where namespaces represent tenants, a deprovisioned tenant could recreate its namespace context.

Exploitation requires: (1) authentication is enabled (the default), (2) the attacker has an active session established before the namespace drop, (3) a root administrator drops the attacker's namespace. HTTP-per-request authentication would fail because the namespace's access method definitions were deleted with the namespace. There is no default session TTL for WebSocket connections.

Setup: A namespace "tenant_a" exists with a database "app" and a DB-level Editor user.
```

2. A root administrator drops the namespace: REMOVE NAMESPACE tenant_a.
3. The DB Editor (session still active) sends: DEFINE FUNCTION fn::test() {RETURN 1}.

```surql

DEFINE USER editor ON DATABASE PASSWORD 'test' ROLES EDITOR;

-- Step 2 (separate session): Editor authenticates
SIGNIN { user: 'editor', pass: 'test', ns: 'tenant_a', db: 'app' };

-- Step 3: Root drops the namespace
REMOVE NAMESPACE tenant_a;

advisories.title: Interactive transactions keep the writes of a statement refused by a THROWing event, and commit persists them
advisories.summary:
### Summary

In an interactive transaction (RPC `begin` / `query` with the transaction id / `commit`), a statement refused by a table event that `THROW`s reports an error, yet its write **and the writes the event made before the `THROW`** stay in the transaction. A subsequent `commit` persists them. The refused statement behaves as if the event's guard had passed.

Events with `THROW` are commonly used as guards (business rules, ownership or access checks). Any client that can open an interactive transaction and has write access to the table can get past such a guard: run the guarded statement, ignore the error, and commit.

For comparison, all three of these leave nothing persisted:
- the same statement outside a transaction;
- the same statement inside a single-request `BEGIN … COMMIT` batch;
- a statement refused by a field `ASSERT` or a type error inside the same interactive transaction.

### Affected versions

Reproduced on SurrealDB **3.3.4** and **3.1.5** (official Docker images, `memory` storage, root session), with the official Python SDK 2.0.0 over WebSocket (RPC `begin`/`commit`). 2.x does not offer interactive transactions over RPC.

### Reproduction

```python
import asyncio, sys, uuid
from surrealdb import AsyncSurreal

async def main(url: str) -> None:
    c = AsyncSurreal(url); await c.connect(); await c.signin({"username": "root", "password": "root"})
    db = "v" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]
    await c.query_raw(f"DEFINE NAMESPACE IF NOT EXISTS probe; USE NS probe; DEFINE DATABASE {db};"); await c.use("probe", db)
    await c.query("DEFINE TABLE item SCHEMALESS; DEFINE EVENT guard ON item WHEN $event = 'CREATE' AND $after.qty < 0 THEN { CREATE audit SET k = 'before-throw'; THROW 'qty must be >= 0' };")
    await c.query("DEFINE TABLE acct SCHEMAFULL; DEFINE FIELD balance ON acct TYPE int ASSERT $value >= 0;")
    cases = {
        "THROW, commit at once": ["CREATE item:bad SET qty = -1"],
        "THROW, then an unrelated OK statement": ["CREATE item:bad SET qty = -1", "CREATE item:ok SET qty = 1"],
        "ASSERT, then an unrelated OK statement": ["CREATE acct:bad SET balance = -5", "CREATE acct:ok SET balance = 1"],
    }
    for label, stmts in cases.items():
        await c.query("DELETE item; DELETE acct; DELETE audit;")
        t = await c.begin()
        st = []
        for s in stmts:
            r = await c.query_raw(s + ";", txn_id=t); st.append(r["result"][0]["status"])
        await c.commit(t)
        rows = await c.query("SELECT VALUE id FROM item, acct, audit;")
        print(f"{label:40} statuses={st} -> after commit: {sorted(str(x) for x in rows)}")
    await c.close()

asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1]))   # e.g. ws://localhost:8000/rpc
```

Output on 3.3.4 (identical on 3.1.5):

```
THROW, commit at once                    statuses=['ERR'] -> after commit: ['audit:…', 'item:bad']
THROW, then an unrelated OK statement    statuses=['ERR', 'OK'] -> after commit: ['audit:…', 'item:bad', 'item:ok']
ASSERT, then an unrelated OK statement   statuses=['ERR', 'OK'] -> after commit: ['acct:ok']
```

Expected: `item:bad` and the event's `audit` row are not persisted, as in the `ASSERT` case and outside transactions. Inside the transaction, the refused record is also visible to later statements: an `UPDATE item:bad …` in the same transaction succeeds.

### Impact

A guard implemented as a `THROW`ing event can be bypassed through an interactive transaction by anyone allowed to write the table. The guarded record, and any side effects the event wrote before throwing, are persisted, with only an error reported for the statement. Clients that catch the statement's error and commit (a common retry or "best effort" pattern) persist them without meaning to.

### Suggested fix

When a statement fails inside an interactive transaction, roll back that statement's writes, including those of its events, as an `ASSERT` failure already does. Alternatively, mark the transaction as failed so that `commit` is refused.

advisories.title: Model Export Route joins Raw Name Permitting Authenticated Request Redirection
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A credential leakage and Server-Side Request Forgery vulnerability exists in SurrealDB's remote HTTP client router (`surrealdb/surrealdb`). In `surrealdb/src/engine/remote/http/mod.rs`, model names are passed directly to `Url::join()` as URL references.

### Vulnerability Details
- Affected File: `surrealdb/src/engine/remote/http/mod.rs` (`router`, `Command::ExportMl`, `Command::ExportBytesMl`)
- Mechanism: `Url::join` treats absolute URLs as target replacements rather than path segments. When exporting a model with a user-supplied name such as `https://attacker.com/ml`, `Url::join` resets the destination origin to the attacker's server. The HTTP client then issues the request to the attacker's server with the current session's authentication tokens and headers attached.
- Impact: Credential disclosure of SurrealDB session tokens and authenticated destination SSRF.

### Recommended Remediation
URL-encode model names before appending them to the path, or use `url.path_segments_mut()` to ensure they are treated strictly as path segments.

---
**Reported by:** ARSB

### Patches

A patch has been created that pins an ML export request to its intended host, so an authenticated request can no longer be redirected to another host.

- Version 4.0.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### References

- [SurrealDB Documentation - Capabilities](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealdb/security/capabilities)
- `fix(sdk): ML export URL lets an authenticated request be redirected to another host` (commit `a44fca7d74`)

advisories.title: UNIQUE-Index Conflict Errors Disclose SELECT-Restricted Field Values and Record Ids in SurrealDB
advisories.summary:
### Summary

When a write conflicts with a UNIQUE index, SurrealDB returns the error `Database index `<index>` already contains `<value>`, with record `<record>`` to the caller verbatim. The message embeds the stored hidden value and the record id of the existing row, and the write path never consults the acting principal's field-level SELECT permissions or the row's table PERMISSIONS before doing so. Any authenticated principal with write access to a table therefore obtains a reliable existence oracle over field values and rows its SELECT permissions forbid reading: a probe write either succeeds (value unused) or returns the hidden value and record id (value in use). Verified on the official v3.3.0 Docker image (2026-09-24, current release) and by source review on main `18971ffb` (2026-09-04).


### Details

SurrealDB treats error text as permission-relevant: GHSA-6g9v-7gq3-p2c6 (fixed 3.1.0) stripped raw operands from arithmetic error messages for exactly this reason, and the September 2026 security wave hardened the indexed read paths (restricted-field indexes withheld from query planning in GHSA-x6mm-9295-rvph; indexed COUNT/ORDER BY fast paths guarded in GHSA-c8j9-96c9-8xrp and GHSA-h4h3-3rfj-x6fq). The unique-index write-conflict path was not covered.

- `surrealdb/core/src/err/mod.rs:541` (main `18971ffb`): `Error::IndexExists { record, index, value }` formats as `Database index `{index}` already contains `{value}`, with record `{record}``.
- Raised by `surrealdb/core/src/idx/index.rs::err_index_exists` (line 398, raise at line 205) during unique-index maintenance in the document write pipeline (`doc/create.rs`, `doc/insert.rs`, `doc/upsert.rs`).
- Nothing on this path consults the acting principal's `PERMISSIONS FOR select` on the field or the table before including the stored value and record id.

Both restriction models are bypassed:

- Field-level: `DEFINE FIELD email ON users PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE` - a principal with CREATE but no SELECT on `email` receives the stored `email` value verbatim in the conflict error.
- Row-level: `DEFINE TABLE secrets PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE` - a principal with INSERT permission on the table receives the fully invisible record's unique field value and its record id.

The uniqueness enforcement itself is correct (the write is rejected); the flaw is the content of the failure observable, which turns a rejected write into a read oracle.

### Proof of concept

Environment: official `surrealdb/surrealdb:latest` image (v3.3.0) on 127.0.0.1:16451, root user bootstraps the schema, a record user `alice` with CREATE/INSERT permission only. All data synthetic. The attached archive automates every step; the container is removed on exit.

Controls: the boundary is real and active - the unauthenticated caller is denied, root sees the protected value, and alice's SELECT reveals nothing:

```text
[PASS] C1 unauthenticated SELECT denied
[PASS] C2 privileged SELECT sees field (schema active)
[PASS] C3 alice SELECT does not reveal protected values
```

Payload A (field-level restriction): `email` carries a UNIQUE index and `PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE`. alice probes with a candidate value:

```text

→ Database index 'users_email_uniq' already contains 'victim@example.com', with record 'users:victim'
[PASS] A1 conflict error echoes probed value + record id (field-restricted)
[PASS] A2 non-conflicting probe succeeds (differential confirmed)
```

The rejected write returns the stored hidden value (`victim@example.com`) and the record id (`users:victim`). A probe with an unused value succeeds, completing the existence oracle.

Payload B (row-level restriction): a fully invisible record `secrets:s1` (table `PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE`) with a UNIQUE field leaks its existence, value echo, and record id the same way:

```text

advisories.title: Re-RELATE on an Existing Edge Echoes Stored in/out Endpoints Despite SELECT Restrictions in SurrealDB
advisories.summary:
### Summary

`RELATE a->edge:existing->b` against an already-stored edge runs the update path and compares the supplied endpoints with the stored ones. On mismatch, the `InOverride`/`OutOverride` error embeds the **stored** endpoint record id - taken from `self.initial.doc.pick(&IN/OUT)` - although the message wording ("which does not match the existing field value") implies the caller-supplied value is echoed. Each mismatched RELATE therefore returns one true endpoint of a hidden edge directly, with no brute force: one query for `in`, one (with a matching `in`) for `out`. Graph structure the caller's SELECT permissions deny is disclosed verbatim, for both row-level (`PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE` on the edge table) and field-level (`DEFINE FIELD in/out ... PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE`) restrictions. Verified on the official v3.3.0 Docker image (2026-09-24, current release) and by source review on main `18971ffb` (2026-09-04).


### Details

The edge-endpoint override check runs in `surrealdb/core/src/doc/alter.rs::default_record_data` (`InOverride`/`OutOverride` arms at v3.3.0 lines 279/296, errors at `doc/error.rs:50-59`; `alter.rs:244` and `err/mod.rs:629` on HEAD), reached from `doc/relate.rs::relate_update`:

```rust
match (self.initial.doc.as_ref().pick(&IN), self.is_new()) {
    (Value::RecordId(id), false) if id == *l => { /* unchanged */ }
    (_, true) => { /* new edge: supplied value stored */ }
    (v, _) => bail!(DocError::InOverride { value: v.to_sql() })   // v = STORED endpoint
}
```

`v` binds from the initial (stored) document and is formatted into the client-visible error without any permission check on `in`/`out` of the stored edge, although the read path demonstrably filters these fields for the same principal (`SELECT in, out FROM <edge>` returns nothing). The newer `RecordExists` guard (the GHSA-f82j-v89j-mf86 fix) does not preempt this path; the caller needs UPDATE permission on the edge, which is exactly what makes the boundary crossing specific - write yes, read no. The message semantics are also inverted relative to the code (it names the stored value), making the error misleading even in normal operation.

### Proof of concept

Environment: official `surrealdb/surrealdb:latest` image (v3.3.0) on 127.0.0.1:16451, root bootstraps the schema, record user `alice` created by the PoC. All data synthetic. The attached archive automates every step and removes its container on exit.

PERMISSIONS FOR select NONE`, seeded with `person:carol->wrote2:edge88->book:diary`.

Controls: the boundary is real and active - root sees both endpoints, alice's SELECT reveals none, and alice may create fresh edges and re-RELATE with matching endpoints:

[PASS] T2 row-hidden edge: error echoes stored 'out' = book:diary
[PASS] T3 field-hidden edge: error echoes stored 'in' = person:carol
```

Each mismatched RELATE returns `Found person:carol for the 'in' field, ...` / `Found book:diary for the 'out' field, ...` - the stored endpoints of an edge whose SELECT returns nothing to alice.

advisories.title: SurrealDB LIVE query notification expressions allow write side effects that bypass the write-blocking guard
advisories.summary:
## Summary

SurrealDB's LIVE query notification pipeline evaluates subscriber-supplied WHERE clauses and field projections with write-blocking disabled, allowing embedded write subqueries (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, RELATE) to execute atomically within other users' triggering transactions. The `permission_predicate` guard introduced in GHSA-66r2-5gwj-gxm2 to block side effects in PERMISSIONS predicates was never extended to LIVE notification expression evaluation, violating a documented security invariant in SECURITY_GUIDE.md that requires these expressions to be side-effect free.

## Root Cause

The write-blocking guard at `surrealdb/core/src/expr/expression.rs:432` rejects mutating statements only when `opt.permission_predicate` is `true`. In the LIVE notification pipeline, `Document::lq_compute` creates the evaluation options via `opt.new_with_perms(true)` (`surrealdb/core/src/doc/lives.rs:109`), which sets the `perms` field but leaves `permission_predicate` at its default `false` (`surrealdb/core/src/dbs/options.rs:66`). The PERMISSIONS predicate evaluation at `lq_allow` (`lives.rs:577`) correctly uses `opt.new_for_permission_predicate()` to enable the guard, but the WHERE clause evaluation (`lq_check` at `lives.rs:539`) and field projection evaluation (`Fields::compute` at `lives.rs:342`) both run with the unguarded options.

```text
Affected functions:
- Document::lq_compute (surrealdb/core/src/doc/lives.rs): creates options with permission_predicate=false (line 109) and evaluates subscriber projections at line 342 without write-blocking
- Document::lq_check (surrealdb/core/src/doc/lives.rs): evaluates subscriber WHERE clause at line 539 with permission_predicate=false; no guard against write subqueries
```

## Impact

An authenticated user with a database-level session, SELECT permission on the watched table (required for LIVE query registration since version 3.1.0), and write permission on a target table can register a LIVE query containing write subqueries in the projection or WHERE clause. When any other user subsequently writes to the watched table, the subscriber's write subqueries execute atomically within the triggering user's transaction.

The subscriber does not gain new write targets; standard table-level permissions (`perms: true`) still apply to the injected writes. The demonstrated capabilities that exceed normal access are:

1. **Transaction injection:** The subscriber's writes execute atomically within another user's transaction, sharing commit and rollback semantics. This is not achievable through independent queries.
2. **Write amplification:** N registered LIVE subscriptions with write expressions multiply write load by N for every triggering event. The triggering user has no visibility into or control over this amplification.
3. **Post-revocation side effects:** Because the WHERE clause evaluates before the PERMISSIONS check (`lq_check` at line 253 runs before `lq_allow` at line 270), write side effects in the WHERE clause that reference document fields can exfiltrate data even after the subscriber's SELECT permission is revoked.

## Proof of Concept

```text
Dependencies: SurrealDB server with auth and realtime enabled (default configuration)
Setup: Two authenticated sessions with database-level access
```

```surql
-- Session A (subscriber): register LIVE query with write subquery in projection
LIVE SELECT *, (CREATE audit CONTENT {source: name, ts: time::now()}) AS exfil FROM person
```

```surql
-- Session B (any user): write to the watched table
CREATE person:1 SET name = 'Alice'
```

```text
-- Expected result on vulnerable version:
-- The LIVE notification pipeline evaluates the projection at lives.rs:342
-- with permission_predicate=false. The CREATE audit subquery passes through
-- expression.rs:432 without hitting the guard, executes under the subscriber's
-- permissions, and commits atomically with Session B's CREATE person:1.
--

advisories.title: ON DELETE REJECT Errors Disclose SELECT-Hidden Referencing Record Ids in SurrealDB
advisories.summary:
### Summary

When SurrealDB rejects a delete because an `ON DELETE REJECT` reference exists, the error reads `Cannot delete `<record>` as it is referenced by `<foreign>` with an ON DELETE REJECT clause` - and `<foreign>` is taken straight from the reference index with no permission gate. A principal who may delete a record but cannot SELECT the rows referencing it learns that a hidden referencing row exists and obtains its exact record id, one candidate record per query. This crosses the row-level SELECT permission boundary of the referencing table (`PERMISSIONS FOR select WHERE public = true` demonstrated, `NONE` equally affected). Verified on the official v3.3.0 Docker image (2026-09-24, current release) and by source review on main `18971ffb` (2026-09-04).


### Details

The reference-integrity check in the delete pipeline, `surrealdb/core/src/doc/purge.rs::check_referenced` (v3.3.0 line 532), scans the reference-index range for the record being deleted and, on the `Reject` strategy, constructs the referencing record id directly from the index key (`key.foreign_table`, `key.foreign_key`) and bails with `DeleteRejectedByReference(rid.to_sql(), record.to_sql())` (error at `doc/error.rs:131` on v3.3.0; `purge.rs:359` and `err/mod.rs:1182` on HEAD). Nothing on this path consults the acting principal's SELECT permissions on the foreign record, although the same principal's SELECT on the referencing table is demonstrably filtered by the row-level predicate (the row is invisible via SELECT), and the error is surfaced as `kind: Internal` - not as a permission error - so callers cannot even distinguish an integrity signal from a denial.

The rejection itself is intended behavior (referential integrity works); the flaw is the content of the failure observable. SurrealDB's own advisory line treats hidden-data-in-error-text as a patchable vulnerability class (GHSA-6g9v-7gq3-p2c6, arithmetic operand echo). The reference/edge advisory family covers only integrity issues (GHSA-4w65-7h3j-p29h CASCADE permission bypass, GHSA-whwg-vh4f-pmmf / CVE-2026-49997 edge delete bypass); no advisory covers this disclosure.

### Proof of concept

Environment: official `surrealdb/surrealdb:latest` image (v3.3.0) on 127.0.0.1:16451, root bootstraps the schema, a record user `alice` is created by the PoC. All data synthetic. The attached archive automates every step and removes its container on exit.

Schema: `asset` with `PERMISSIONS FULL`; `report` with `PERMISSIONS FOR select WHERE public = true, FOR create FULL, FOR update FULL, FOR delete NONE` and `DEFINE FIELD about TYPE record<asset> REFERENCE ON DELETE REJECT`; one hidden referencing row (`report:case_hidden`, `public = false`) pointing at `asset:doc_secret`, one public row, one unreferenced asset.

Controls: the boundary is real and active - the unauthenticated caller is denied, root sees both rows, alice's SELECT returns only the public row, and alice can delete an unreferenced asset:

```text

[PASS] C1 privileged caller sees hidden row (fixture valid)
[PASS] C2 alice SELECT shows only public row (boundary holds on SELECT)
[PASS] C3 alice DELETE of unreferenced record succeeds
```

Payload: alice deletes the referenced `asset:doc_secret`:

```text
[PASS] T1 reject error discloses SELECT-hidden record id 'report:case_hidden'
[PASS] T1b error surfaced as Internal (not a permission denial)
[PASS] T2 control: root's delete rejected by REJECT clause too
```
